newsitem.title: CHILE: Rallying Chilean shares push still higher.
newsitem.headline: Rallying Chilean shares push still higher.

text.p: Chilean blue chips, already at record highs, stormed higher on confidence that a drought parching central Chile is over and on expectations of strong economic growth for the rest of the year, brokers said.

The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares was at 129.65 points, up 1.96 percent for the day led by electricals. Utility stocks had plummetted on concerns over that a lack of precipitation would could force them to buy more fossil fuel as their hydroelectric output fell.

Nonstop rain in Santiago for the past 40 hours was enough to convince the market that the drought, Chile's worst since the 1960s, was now history, brokers said. So much rain fell Thursday and Friday that precipitation levels for the year are now above normal.
Power generator Endesa, vulnerable to the drought because of its dams, was up 4.3 percent to 304 pesos and its parent company Enersis was up 2.5 percent to 280 pesos.
Brokers reported strong demand from both foreign and local investors amid feverish, high-volume trade. The all-share IGPA index was up 1.36 percent to 5638.16 points.
The market was also buoyed by comments by Economy Minister Alvaro Garca, who said the economy would grow by at least six percent in the second half of the year, said brokers.
